extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, NIH/program officers, and collaborators evaluating the Facilities & Other Resources section of a grant proposal
extracted.subtask_description: The Facilities & Other Resources narrative describing institutional environment, physical space, laboratory capacity, cores, library access, administrative support, and training resources provided to support the proposed project (as in an NIH R01 application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional research environment and stature
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of Washington (UW) provides an excellent environment for training and research characterized by recent growth, diversity and excellence in all types of health-related research and education. The University has been the top public university in federal research funding every year since 1974 and among the top five universities, public and private, in federal funding since 1969.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows breadth/depth of faculty (~3,900 teaching and research faculty), long-standing federal funding record, interdisciplinary collaborations across schools (Medicine, Public Health, Pharmacy, Nursing, Social Work, Dentistry, Arts & Sciences, Business, Law, Public Affairs). Useful evidence for reviewers about institutional commitment and capacity to support high-quality research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical office and meeting space (ICRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC offices are located on the 12th floor of the Ninth & Jefferson building (NJB) with approximately 6,000 sq. ft. dedicated to ICRC office space for investigators and administrative staff, providing for 30 faculty, visiting scientists, staff, and students. Ten conference rooms on the 12th and 13th floors are available for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on square footage, capacity, office configuration (private enclosed offices for faculty, grouped staff by function) and availability of multiple conference rooms support claims of sufficient workspace and local meeting/training capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wired and wireless networking and computing access
rubrics_metrics.description: All offices and conference rooms are wired with T-100 Ethernet cabling and dual voice/data communication capabilities. Secure Wi-Fi access is available. Each UW investigator and staff member has Ethernet access, and the UW mainframe computer is available to investigators and staff, providing access to online reference services, websites, and databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates connectivity and computing infrastructure necessary for data work, remote collaboration, and accessing online resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiovisual and videoconferencing facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference rooms include data, phone, and projector connections; select rooms include wall-mounted LCD monitors and Polycom videoconferencing capabilities. One classroom is fully-equipped for distance learning with ceiling-hung projector, lectern, ceiling-mounted camera, boundary microphones, Polycom videoconferencing, live webcasting, webinar, and lecture capture capability. One videoconferencing suite includes a dedicated Polycom system with 80-port hub, wall-mounted camera configured for enhanced telepresence, and two wall-mounted LCD monitors supporting up to 80 H.323-compliant clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies AV and telepresence capacity for large-scale remote meetings, trainings, and multi-site collaborations — relevant for proposals requiring remote coordination or distance education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory space and biosafety containment
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC Laboratory is an 850 sq. ft. laboratory containing bench and desk space with computer work stations. The lab space is sectioned into BSL1 for contained specimen handling and BSL2 where a 4-ft. biological safety cabinet is available for appropriate containment for clinical (HSV and HIV-positive) sample manipulations. Access to the University of Washington Retrovirology Laboratory (Dr. Robert Coombs, Director) is available for any laboratory activities that require BSL3 containment, such as plasma viral loads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete biosafety level capabilities and physical lab footprint; reviewers assess whether biosafety and lab infrastructure meet project needs. Explicit mention of BSL3 access is important when higher containment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central specimen repository and freezer capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICRC Central Specimen Repository houses samples from multiple HIV prevention research studies. The Repository includes space for (48) -80°C and -20°C freezers in the Freezer Farm, located on the second parking level. This storage facility can store 2.6 million specimens. Each freezer is equipped with an alarm to track temperature variations. Data Capture software is used to manage temperature and immediately alert staff to adverse conditions. This system operates nonstop and has a built-in power backup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights specimen storage capacity, monitoring/alerting systems, data capture, and power backup — key criteria for sample integrity and long-term biobanking support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative, grant, and research support services
rubrics_metrics.description: The UW research infrastructure offers a wide array of services to support researchers—including technology transfer, human subjects review, and grant and contract services. Centrally-located administrative offices house main administrative staff including administrative systems manager and grants operation manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates availability of institutional offices and staff to assist with contracts, compliance, and grant administration; reviewers consider this when evaluating project feasibility and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support services and core technical shops
rubrics_metrics.description: Support services available include a machine shop, electronics shop, computer graphics services, photographic services, and financial management services. There is daily courier service between UW, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Harborview Medical Center, and several clinics and research sites to transport specimens and materials between clinics and laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates practical operational supports (fabrication, imaging, specimen transport) that facilitate project logistics and timely sample handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for early-stage investigators and career development
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of Washington is committed to the development of early stage investigators. The ICRC conducts weekly work in progress meetings for early stage investigators to receive feedback on their research and has outstanding support for administration of study projects. The Department of Global Health, UW and Fred Hutch CFAR conduct career enrichment workshops and seminars, facilitate formal peer groups and provide support and instruction for conducting research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows mentoring, peer feedback, workshops, and institutional programs that support trainee career development — relevant to mentorship and training plan evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to interdisciplinary departments and faculty expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant Schools and Departments at UW include the School of Public Health (Departments of Epidemiology, Global Health, Biostatistics, Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences, Health Services), Division of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine, Department of Epidemiology, and Department of Global Health with numerous faculty and centers covering a broad range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates availability of domain expertise (epidemiology, biostatistics, infectious diseases, implementation science) and breadth of faculty for collaboration and mentoring; reviewers use this to judge scientific environment strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional centers, cores, and collaborative programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Major research centers and service programs include: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), Center for AIDS Research (CFAR), Kenya Research and Training Center, International Training and Education Center for Health (I-TECH), Global WACh, PERLA, Global Medicines Program, Center for Health and the Global Environment, and Health Alliance International (HAI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of specialized centers and NIH-funded infrastructure (e.g., CFAR) provides core support, collaborative networks, and shared resources that strengthen project feasibility and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library resources, access to literature, and document delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The UW library system houses more than seven million volumes and 62,000 current serials. Health Sciences Libraries include more than 350,000 bound volumes and about 2,400 current journal subscriptions. Desktop access (including remote/off-campus) to thousands of electronic journals is available to UW investigators at no cost. Document delivery via e-mail for items not available electronically is available 24 hours a day with normal (within 24 hours) or rush (within 4 hours) turn-around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates immediate access to literature and rapid document delivery supporting timely background research and evidence gathering for the project.
